background: In September 2026, UK education software provider Bromcom suffered a data breach involving a legacy single sign-on (SSO) registration system . The incident exposed 355k unique email addresses belonging to staff and pupils at UK schools, alongside SSO registration reference numbers. Bromcom confirmed that no passwords or authentication tokens were exposed, and that the incident did not enable access to Microsoft or Google accounts or its school management system.
how: The published account does not explain the exact way the data was obtained.
outcome: Have I Been Pwned lists 355,051 email addresses in this breach record. An address total measures the source record's coverage.
The reported exposed data includes Email addresses.

fields.name: Email addresses
fields.why: An exposed address may be used in phishing attempts. Treat unexpected messages with caution.

actions: Be alert to phishing. A message may use details from exposed or collected records to appear familiar; verify requests through the service directly.
